$about: The whitelist §1.2 of 05-architecture.md asks for, made real.
§1.1 gives four independent, register-anchored reasons why application data
must NOT travel through UI-route loaders: the 5000 ms client-held move that
must produce zero requests when undone; per-block error boundaries that a
page-level loader cannot express; one shared poll scheduler that
useRevalidator cannot address selectively; and the sendBeacon flush, which
posts a Blob to a URL and can only talk to a resource route.
§1.2 then whitelists exactly ONE: the pipeline route's first paint carries
real board data, because that is what makes LCP reachable with 500 leads.
'The whitelist is a single-entry versioned file; adding a second entry is a
PR that touches that file and nothing else.'
THE FILE DID NOT EXIST, so the count drifted with nothing to notice. Three
data loaders are live where the ruling sanctions one. This file makes that
visible and scripts/ui-loader-whitelist.test.ts makes a FOURTH impossible to
`navigation` entries are not part of the count and are not an exemption: a
loader that resolves identity and redirects carries no application data, so
none of §1.1's four reasons apply to it.

routes.reason: §1.2's single entry. The pipeline's first paint must carry real board data — it is the screen that carries the LCP budget at 500 leads, and a rendered-but-empty shell pays the SSR cost for nothing. Its loader body is one call to the same readPipeline the /api/board resource route calls, so it is not a second implementation.

Calls readBoard directly. It also polls /api/leaderboard client-side, so the loader buys the first paint and nothing else. CORRECTED 2026-08-03: this entry used to justify itself as the demo's opening moment, 'where DEMO-10 wants rank and gap above the fold inside ten seconds'. That is no longer true and was never quite right — §7 puts the first ten seconds on the SELLER HOME, and home.tsx redirects to My Day. The rank and gap now render there, in a block that fetches its own data. What this loader still buys is the first paint of /earnings, which is the demo's SECOND screen (DEMO-01).
routes.decision: OPEN — Jorge's, and the case for keeping it is weaker than this file used to claim. Either drop the loader and accept a skeleton on the second screen, or promote this to a second sanctioned entry with a reason that survives the correction above.

routes.reason: Calls readMyDay directly. This one has the weakest case: §1.1 reason 2 names My Day explicitly — every block is an independent fetch with its own error and its own retry, so a failed rank block must not take My Day down. A page-level loader is precisely the pattern the register forbids there.
routes.decision: OPEN — the strongest candidate for removal of the three, on the register's own wording.

routes.reason: Resolves identity and redirects when there is no session. Carries no application data, and the redirect belongs here precisely so it is written once instead of repeated per screen.
Redirects to My Day when there is a session and to sign-in when there is not. No data.
